Folduo adds fold animations alongside your existing launcher. As the phone folds, the display moves like frosted glass while the image appears to stay behind it. Close the phone fully once after starting to finish setup. While active, the cover remains the primary display and apps move between the two screens. The held image gives way to the live app when its display is ready.

The inner screen has Back, Home, Recent apps and Settings controls at the bottom. Tap a card in Recent apps to switch apps. The bar sits over the app without resizing it and hides during folding. The cover uses Samsung’s normal navigation. The status bar clock and notification icons also hide during transitions. The inner controls are provided by Folduo; they do not restore Samsung’s notification panel or gestures.
Start Shizuku using wireless debugging on your phone, then grant Folduo access. Shizuku needs to be started again after a reboot.

While enabled, Folduo temporarily captures other apps during folding and displays the image with angle-dependent parallax and blur. Images are used only in memory and released when a transition ends, the animation stops, or the phone locks. They are never saved or sent anywhere. Protected screens are not captured.

Both displays stay on while enabled, using more battery. Normal display control resumes when you stop Folduo or lock the phone. Stop any older angle helper before starting. If another process is already controlling the displays, Folduo will show the reason instead of starting.

Folduo normally reconnects automatically. You can also tap Resume in the notification. Unlock the phone and close it fully once. After a reboot, start Shizuku first. If you force-stop Folduo or stop it from Android’s list of active apps, resume it from this screen.
Set battery use to “Unrestricted” for Folduo and Shizuku to reduce background interruptions. Screen capture and fold animations pause while the screen is off.
